title: Equation-count comparison quotient at a finitely presented syntomic prime
statement: Let $R$ and $S$ be commutative rings with an $R$-algebra structure, $S$ finitely presented over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra], and $q\in\operatorname{Spec}S$ with $p=q\cap R$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Assume $R_p\to S_q$ is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] and the canonical fibre prime $Q=\ker(\kappa(p)\otimes_R S\to\kappa(q))$ has a principal neighbourhood which is a global complete intersection over $\kappa(p)$ [def-weil-pbc-complete-intersection-over-field]. There exist natural numbers $n,c$, equations $f:\{1,\ldots,c\}\to R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], a surjective $R$-algebra map $\pi:T=R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(f)\to S$, and $u\in T$ with $\pi(u)\notin q$, such that the canonical map $T_u\to S_{\pi(u)}$ is bijective [def-weil-ring-localization-away]. With $q_T=\pi^{-1}(q)$ and $p_T=q_T\cap R$, one has $c\le n$ and the topological dimension at the canonical prime of $\kappa(p_T)\otimes_R T$ is $n-c$ [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point].

proof.text: (Presentation and the fibre.) By [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra] choose $n\ge0$ and $a_1,\dots,a_m\in P=R[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] with $S\cong P/I$, $I=(a_1,\dots,a_m)$; let $\pi:P\to S$ be the quotient map and $\mathfrak q'=\pi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$, a prime of $P$ containing $I$ whose inverse image in $R$ is $\mathfrak p$. Let $\rho:P\to k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ be the coefficient reduction along $R\to R_{\mathfrak p}\to k$; $\ker(R\to k)=\mathfrak p$. Let $\bar I=(\rho(a_1),\dots,\rho(a_m))\subseteq k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$, the ideal generated by $\rho(I)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-scalar-extension] $P\otimes_Rk\cong k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$, $p\otimes\lambda\mapsto\lambda\rho(p)$, and by associativity of $\otimes$ and [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-quotient-base-change] (with $A=P$, $B=k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$) $F=(P/I)\otimes_Rk\cong k[x_1,\dots,x_n]/\bar I=:\bar F$ as $k$-algebras, $(a\bmod I)\otimes\lambda\mapsto\lambda\rho(a)\bmod\bar I$. Let $\bar{\mathfrak Q}\subset\bar F$ be the image of $\mathfrak Q$ and $\bar{\mathfrak q}'\subset k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ its inverse image, i.e. the kernel of the $k$-algebra map $\psi:k[x_1,\dots,x_n]\to\bar F\cong F\to\kappa(\mathfrak q)$; it is a prime containing $\bar I$, and $\psi(x_i)$ is the class of $\pi(x_i)$ in $\kappa(\mathfrak q)$. For $a\in P$, $\psi(\rho(a))$ is the image of $(\pi(a))\otimes1$ in $\kappa(\mathfrak q)$, i.e. the class of $\pi(a)$, which vanishes iff $\pi(a)\in\mathfrak q$; hence $\rho^{-1}(\bar{\mathfrak q}')=\mathfrak q'$, so $\rho(P\setminus\mathfrak q')\subseteq k[x_1,\dots,x_n]\setminus\bar{\mathfrak q}'$.

proof.text: (The conormal module of the fibre at $\bar{\mathfrak Q}$ is free of rank $c$.) By hypothesis (3) there is $h\in F\setminus\mathfrak Q$ with $F_h$ a global complete intersection over $k$; its image $\bar h\in\bar F\setminus\bar{\mathfrak Q}$ has $\bar F_{\bar h}\cong F_h$ as $k$-algebras, so $\bar F_{\bar h}$ is a global complete intersection [def-weil-pbc-complete-intersection-over-field]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-lci-conormal-free-rank-codimension] to $k$, $n$, the ideal $\bar I\subseteq k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$, $\bar F=k[x_1,\dots,x_n]/\bar I$, the prime $\bar{\mathfrak Q}$ and the element $\bar h$: $d:=\dim_{\bar{\mathfrak Q}}(\operatorname{Spec}\bar F)$ [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point] is an integer with $0\le d\le n$, and with $c:=n-d$ the localization $(\bar I/\bar I^2)_{\bar{\mathfrak Q}}$ is a free $\bar F_{\bar{\mathfrak Q}}$-module of rank $c$. (This is condition (4) of Lemma 00SC, which Lemma 00SG yields from condition (3) of 00SG.)

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00SY (lemma-syntomic), proof of (3) => (2), lines 36903-36945 ('By Lemma 00SG the equivalent conditions of Lemma 00SC hold for I-bar and q-bar''); Lemma Tag 00SG (lemma-lci-at-prime, line 36160), (3) => (4); Lemma Tag 00SC (lemma-lci, line 35909), (1) => (4)

proof.text: (Choice of $f_1,\dots,f_c$.) Let $L=k[x_1,\dots,x_n]_{\bar{\mathfrak q}'}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], a local ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m=\bar{\mathfrak q}'L$ and residue field $\kappa=L/\mathfrak m$, and $\bar IL$ the ideal generated by $\bar I$. The image of $k[x_1,\dots,x_n]\setminus\bar{\mathfrak q}'$ in $\bar F$ is $\bar F\setminus\bar{\mathfrak Q}$, so localizing at either gives the same modules [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]; localizing the exact sequences $0\to\bar I^2\to\bar I\to\bar I/\bar I^2\to0$ and $0\to\bar I\to k[x]\to\bar F\to0$ [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-exact] gives $(\bar I/\bar I^2)_{\bar{\mathfrak Q}}\cong\bar IL/\bar I^2L$ over $\bar F_{\bar{\mathfrak Q}}\cong L/\bar IL$. Reducing modulo $\mathfrak m$ and using $\bar I^2L\subseteq\mathfrak m\bar IL$ (as $\bar I\subseteq\bar{\mathfrak q}'$), step 3 shows that $\bar IL/\mathfrak m\bar IL$ is a $\kappa$-vector space of dimension $c$ (a free module of rank $c$ reduces to $\kappa^{\oplus c}$). It is spanned by the classes of $\rho(a_1)/1,\dots,\rho(a_m)/1$, which generate $\bar IL$; choose among them a basis, and let $f_1,\dots,f_c\in\{a_1,\dots,a_m\}\subseteq I$ be the corresponding elements, $\bar f_j=\rho(f_j)$. Since $\bar IL$ is a finitely generated module over the local ring $L$, [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-local-generators] shows that $\bar f_1/1,\dots,\bar f_c/1$ generate $\bar IL$: $\bar IL=(\bar f_1,\dots,\bar f_c)L$.

Pick f_1,...,f_c in I mapping to a basis ... The images f-bar_j generate I-bar_{q-bar'}'); the generation is Nakayama, Lemma Tag 00DV (lemma-NAK)

proof.text: (The comparison ring $S'$.) Let $S'=P/(f_1,\dots,f_c)$ with quotient map $\pi'$. Since $(f_1,\dots,f_c)\subseteq I$, $\pi$ factors as $P\to S'\to S$ with $S'\to S$ surjective with kernel $J=I/(f_1,\dots,f_c)$, a $P$-module generated by the classes $\bar a_1,\dots,\bar a_m$. Let $\mathfrak q'_{S'}=\pi'(\mathfrak q')$, the inverse image of $\mathfrak q$ in $S'$ (a prime). Let $U=P\setminus\mathfrak q'$ and localize the exact sequence of $P$-modules $0\to J\to S'\to S\to0$ at $U$ [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-exact]: $0\to U^{-1}J\to U^{-1}S'\to U^{-1}S\to0$ is exact. As $\pi(U)=S\setminus\mathfrak q$ and $\pi'(U)=S'\setminus\mathfrak q'_{S'}$, $U^{-1}S=S_{\mathfrak q}$ and $U^{-1}S'=S'_{\mathfrak q'_{S'}}$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]. Localizing $0\to I\to P\to S\to0$ and $0\to(f)\to P\to S'\to0$ likewise gives $S_{\mathfrak q}=P_{\mathfrak q'}/IP_{\mathfrak q'}$ and $U^{-1}S'=P_{\mathfrak q'}/(f)P_{\mathfrak q'}$, the map between them being the projection. All these are $P_{\mathfrak q'}$-modules, hence $R_{\mathfrak p}$-modules via $R_{\mathfrak p}\to P_{\mathfrak q'}$ (defined because $R\setminus\mathfrak p$ maps into $U$).

proof.text: (Flatness: the sequence stays exact modulo $\mathfrak p$.) By hypothesis (2), $S_{\mathfrak q}$ is a flat $R_{\mathfrak p}$-module [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-quotient-tensor-injective] over the ring $R_{\mathfrak p}$ to the exact sequence $0\to U^{-1}J\to U^{-1}S'\to S_{\mathfrak q}\to0$ of step 5 with $N=k=R_{\mathfrak p}/\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p}$: $0\to k\otimes_{R_{\mathfrak p}}U^{-1}J\to k\otimes_{R_{\mathfrak p}}U^{-1}S'\to k\otimes_{R_{\mathfrak p}}S_{\mathfrak q}\to0$ is exact. By [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-over-quotient-ring] (1) (ring $R_{\mathfrak p}$, ideal $\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p}$), $k\otimes_{R_{\mathfrak p}}M\cong M/\mathfrak pM$ by $\bar r\otimes x\mapsto rx$, compatibly with linear maps $M\to M'$; so $0\to U^{-1}J/\mathfrak pU^{-1}J\to U^{-1}S'/\mathfrak pU^{-1}S'\to S_{\mathfrak q}/\mathfrak pS_{\mathfrak q}\to0$ is exact.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00SY (lemma-syntomic), proof of (3) => (2), lines 36903-36945 ('As S_q is flat over R we see that J_{q'} (x)_R k -> S'_{q'} (x)_R k is injective (Lemma 00HL)'); Lemma Tag 00HL (lemma-flat-tor-zero, line 9037)

proof.text: (The fibres of $S'$ and $S$ agree at $\mathfrak q'$.) By step 5, the middle map of step 6 is the projection $P_{\mathfrak q'}/((f)P_{\mathfrak q'}+\mathfrak pP_{\mathfrak q'})\to P_{\mathfrak q'}/(IP_{\mathfrak q'}+\mathfrak pP_{\mathfrak q'})$; it is injective iff $IP_{\mathfrak q'}\subseteq(f)P_{\mathfrak q'}+\mathfrak pP_{\mathfrak q'}$. Let $\sigma:P_{\mathfrak q'}\to L$, $a/u\mapsto\rho(a)/\rho(u)$, well defined since $\rho(U)\cap\bar{\mathfrak q}'=\emptyset$ (step 2). (i) $\ker\sigma=\mathfrak pP_{\mathfrak q'}$: $\rho$ kills $\mathfrak pP$; if $\rho(a)/\rho(u)=0$ then $w\rho(a)=0$ for some $w\notin\bar{\mathfrak q}'$, and $k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ is a domain, so $\rho(a)=0$, i.e. every coefficient of $a$ lies in $\ker(R\to k)=\mathfrak p$, so $a\in\mathfrak pP$ and $a/u\in\mathfrak pP_{\mathfrak q'}$. (ii) $\sigma$ is surjective: every element of $k=R_{\mathfrak p}/\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p}$ is the class of some $r/s$ ($r\in R$, $s\in R\setminus\mathfrak p$); taking for $s$ the product of the denominators of the finitely many coefficients, any $y\in k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ is $y=\rho(s)^{-1}\rho(y')$ with $y'\in P$, $s\in R\setminus\mathfrak p$; for $y/w\in L$ write likewise $w=\rho(t)^{-1}\rho(w')$; then $\rho(w')=\rho(t)w\notin\bar{\mathfrak q}'$ (as $\rho(t)\in k^\times$), so $w'\in U$ by step 2, $sw'\in U$, and $\sigma(y't/(w's))=\rho(y')\rho(t)/(\rho(w')\rho(s))=(\rho(s)y)\rho(t)/((\rho(t)w)\rho(s))=y/w$. (iii) For $b\in I$, $\sigma(b/1)=\rho(b)/1\in\bar IL=(\bar f_1,\dots,\bar f_c)L$ (step 4), say $\rho(b)/1=\sum_j\ell_j\bar f_j$ with $\ell_j\in L$; by (ii) $\ell_j=\sigma(z_j)$, so $b/1-\sum_jz_jf_j\in\ker\sigma=\mathfrak pP_{\mathfrak q'}$ by (i). Hence $IP_{\mathfrak q'}\subseteq(f)P_{\mathfrak q'}+\mathfrak pP_{\mathfrak q'}$ and the middle map of step 6 is injective (it is also surjective), so by exactness in step 6, $U^{-1}J/\mathfrak pU^{-1}J=0$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00SY (lemma-syntomic), proof of (3) => (2), lines 36903-36945 ('However, by construction S'_{q'} (x)_R k maps isomorphically to S_q (x)_R k. Hence we conclude that J_{q'} (x)_R k = J_{q'}/pJ_{q'} = 0'); the isomorphism 'by construction' is written out here

proof.text: (Nakayama: $S'$ and $S$ agree near $\mathfrak q'$.) By step 7, $U^{-1}J=\mathfrak pU^{-1}J\subseteq(\mathfrak q'P_{\mathfrak q'})U^{-1}J$, since the image of $\mathfrak p$ in $P$ lies in $\mathfrak q'$. $U^{-1}J$ is a finitely generated $P_{\mathfrak q'}$-module (by the $\bar a_i/1$), and $\mathfrak q'P_{\mathfrak q'}$ is the maximal ideal of the local ring $P_{\mathfrak q'}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], hence its Jacobson radical; by [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-jacobson] $U^{-1}J=0$. So $\bar a_i/1=0$, i.e. $u_i\bar a_i=0$ for some $u_i\in U$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]; $u=u_1\cdots u_m\in U$ (a prime's complement is multiplicative) and $uJ=0$. Localizing $0\to J\to S'\to S\to0$ at $\{u^N\}$ [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-exact] gives $J_u=0$, so the induced $R$-algebra map $S'_{\pi'(u)}\to S_{\pi(u)}$ is an isomorphism; here $\pi'(u)\notin\mathfrak q'_{S'}$ and $\pi(u)\notin\mathfrak q$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00SY (lemma-syntomic), proof of (3) => (2), lines 36903-36945 ('By Nakayama's lemma (Lemma 00DV) we conclude that there exists a g in R[x_1,...,x_n], g not in q' such that J_g = 0. In other words S'_g = S_g'); Lemma Tag 00DV (lemma-NAK)

proof.text: (The fibre of $S'$ has dimension $n-c$ at $\mathfrak q'_{S'}$.) As in step 2, $F'=S'\otimes_Rk\cong\bar F':=k[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(\bar f_1,\dots,\bar f_c)$ [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-scalar-extension] [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-quotient-base-change]. Since $S'/\mathfrak q'_{S'}=P/\mathfrak q'=S/\mathfrak q$, $\kappa(\mathfrak q'_{S'})=\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ compatibly with $S'\to S$, and the composite $k[x_1,\dots,x_n]\to\bar F'\cong F'\to\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ is the $k$-algebra map sending $x_i$ to the class of $\pi(x_i)$, i.e. it is $\psi$ of step 2; so the kernel $\mathfrak Q'$ of $F'\to\kappa(\mathfrak q'_{S'})$ corresponds to $\bar{\mathfrak Q}'=\bar{\mathfrak q}'/(\bar f)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-quotient-dimension-at-point-height-difference], applied to $\bar F=k[x]/\bar I$ at $\bar{\mathfrak Q}$ and to $\bar F'=k[x]/(\bar f)$ at $\bar{\mathfrak Q}'$ (both with inverse image $\bar{\mathfrak q}'$ in $k[x]$): $\dim_{\bar{\mathfrak Q}}\operatorname{Spec}\bar F=n-\operatorname{ht}\bar{\mathfrak q}'+\operatorname{ht}\bar{\mathfrak Q}$ and $\dim_{\bar{\mathfrak Q}'}\operatorname{Spec}\bar F'=n-\operatorname{ht}\bar{\mathfrak q}'+\operatorname{ht}\bar{\mathfrak Q}'$. The chains of primes of $\bar F$ (resp. $\bar F'$) inside $\bar{\mathfrak Q}$ (resp. $\bar{\mathfrak Q}'$) are the chains of primes $\mathfrak P$ of $k[x]$ with $\bar I\subseteq\mathfrak P\subseteq\bar{\mathfrak q}'$ (resp. $(\bar f)\subseteq\mathfrak P\subseteq\bar{\mathfrak q}'$), and for a prime $\mathfrak P\subseteq\bar{\mathfrak q}'$ the two conditions agree: $(\bar f)\subseteq\bar I$; conversely if $(\bar f)\subseteq\mathfrak P$ and $b\in\bar I$, then by step 4 $b/1=\sum_j(y_j/w_j)\bar f_j$ in $L$, so $vw_1\cdots w_cb\in(\bar f)\subseteq\mathfrak P$ for some $v\notin\bar{\mathfrak q}'$ (definition of equality of fractions [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]), and $vw_1\cdots w_c\notin\mathfrak P$ (it is not in $\bar{\mathfrak q}'\supseteq\mathfrak P$), so $b\in\mathfrak P$. Hence $\operatorname{ht}\bar{\mathfrak Q}=\operatorname{ht}\bar{\mathfrak Q}'$ and $\dim_{\mathfrak Q'}\operatorname{Spec}F'=\dim_{\bar{\mathfrak Q}'}\operatorname{Spec}\bar F'=d=n-c$ [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point] (isomorphic rings have homeomorphic spectra).

lean.statement:
theorem exists_equationCount_comparison_of_syntomicAtPrime
    {R : Type u} {S : Type v} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    (q : PrimeSpectrum S)
    (hfp : FinitePresentation R S)
    (hflat : (Localization.localRingHom (q.asIdeal.comap (algebraMap R S)) q.asIdeal
      (algebraMap R S) rfl).Flat)
    (hci : ∃ h : (q.asIdeal.comap (algebraMap R S)).Fiber S,
      h ∉ (PrimeSpectrum.preimageEquivFiber R S (q.comap (algebraMap R S))
        ⟨q, rfl⟩).asIdeal ∧
      IsGlobalCompleteIntersection (q.asIdeal.comap (algebraMap R S)).ResidueField
        (Localization.Away h)) :
    ∃ (n c : ℕ) (f : Fin c → MvPolynomial (Fin n) R),
      let T := MvPolynomial (Fin n) R ⧸ Ideal.span (Set.range f)
      ∃ (π : T →ₐ[R] S) (u : T),
        Function.Surjective π ∧ π u ∉ q.asIdeal ∧
        Function.Bijective
          (IsLocalization.Away.mapₐ (Localization.Away u) (Localization.Away (π u)) π u) ∧
        c ≤ n ∧
        topologicalKrullDimAt
          (PrimeSpectrum.preimageEquivFiber R T
            ((q.comap π.toRingHom).comap (algebraMap R T))
            ⟨q.comap π.toRingHom, rfl⟩) = (n - c : ℕ)
